method.value: Rotate image by 23 deg; second derivative inflection gives cavity edges; fit straight line to half-width vs height; deconvolve in quadrature

evidence.quote: We computed a second-order differential along the x-axis, and the inflection points (where the second-order derivative equals zero) delineate the edge of the cavity.

findings_qualitative.value: Higher-excitation H2 is more collimated and faster, consistent with nested MHD disk wind; CO is slower entrained gas

evidence.quote: The lower velocity mm CO may be gas from the infalling envelope accelerated outwards by the wide angle wind along the cavity walls.

claims.hypothesis: Outflow opening angle depends on excitation
claims.experiment: Measured cavity edges of H2 S(J) and 12CO
claims.result: 40–35 deg for low-J and CO to 28–19 deg for S(7)–S(11)

evidence.quote: the opening angle decreases from 40–35$^\circ$ for the low-J H$_2$ lines (up to S(5))

claims.finding: Consistent with MHD disk wind over X-wind/photoevaporation

evidence.quote: This is consistent with the results of MHD wind simulations, which predicts faster speeds for more collimated parts of the flow

claims.hypothesis: H2 outflow base width compared to disk
claims.result: ≤35 au vs ~30 au disk, 20–23 au jet
claims.finding: Wind wider than jet, comparable to disk

evidence.quote: The outflow width (as traced in H$_2$ 0-0 S(11)) at the protostellar location measures $\leq$35 au

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Photoevaporative wind disfavoured (low molecular fraction, velocities <10 km/s, weak UV in quiescent phase)

evidence.quote: IRAS 16253-2429 is currently in a quiescent phase and is therefore unlikely to possess a sufficiently strong UV field to drive photoevaporation.
